Structures in PIF: Standardized JSON for Biological Data

Source: vignettes/structs.Rmd
structs.Rmd

Introduction

The PIFDataModel package is designed to standardize data storage and handling for biological studies, particularly focusing on structured JSON schemas. This vignette provides an overview of the available data structures (structs), their purposes, and examples of how to access and utilize them.

Struct Categories

Below is an overview of the structs included in the PIFDataModel package:

Category Name Description Link
Bacteria Count Data Contains bacteria count information View
General Data Contains general information about bacteria View
Full Structure Represents the complete bacteria structure View
Prevalence Data Contains data on bacteria prevalence View
Results Data Stores results related to bacteria analysis View
Tree Defines the hierarchical tree structure of bacteria View
FAO Information Provides information related to FAO View
Tree Represents the hierarchical structure of FAO View
Food Characteristics Contains details about food characteristics View
Tree Represents the hierarchical structure of food View
Nematodes General Data Contains general information about nematodes View
Essay Identification Tree Represents essay data for identifying nematodes View
Essay Infectivity Tree Represents essay data for nematodes infectivity View
Essay Sample Tree Represents essay data for nematode samples View
Full Structure Represents the complete nematodes structure View
Food Information Provides nematodes-related information for food View
Prevalence Enumeration Results Data Contains prevalence enumeration results for nematodes View
Prevalence Results Data Stores prevalence results for nematodes analysis View
Results Data Stores results related to nematodes analysis View
Subtype Tree Defines the subtype tree for nematodes View
Tree Defines the hierarchical tree structure of nematodes View
Protozoans Essay Identification Tree Represents essay data for identifying protozoans View
Essay Infectivity Tree Represents essay data for protozoans infectivity View
Essay Sample Tree Represents essay data for protozoan samples View
Full Structure Represents the complete protozoans structure View
Parasite Data Contains data related to protozoan parasites View
Parasite Tree Represents the hierarchical structure of parasites View
Prevalence Enumeration Results Data Contains prevalence enumeration results for protozoans View
Results Data Stores results related to protozoans analysis View
Subtype Tree Defines the subtype tree for protozoans View
Virus Essay Identification Tree Represents essay data for identifying viruses View
Essay Infectivity Tree Represents essay data for virus infectivity View
Full Structure Represents the complete virus structure View
Prevalence Enumeration Results Data Contains prevalence enumeration results for viruses View
Results Infectivity Data Stores results related to virus infectivity View
Results Quality Data Stores quality results for virus analysis View
Subtype Tree Defines the subtype tree for viruses View
Study Struct Provides the struct for study data View

Examples

Here are examples of how to load and work with the structs in R:

Loading the PIFDataModel Package 

# Load the PIFDataModel package
library(PIFDataModel)

Accessing the Bacteria Count Data Struct 

library(jsonlite)
# Load the JSON struct
bacteria_struct <- jsonlite::read_json("../inst/data/valid_sample_data.json")

# Print the struct
print(bacteria_struct)
## $SampleWEnum
## [1] 1
## 
## $LoQ
## [1] 2
## 
## $GreaterLoQ
## [1] 3
## 
## $LowerLoQ
## [1] 4
## 
## $MeanConc
## [1] 5
## 
## $CountsModel
## [1] "Impute"

Example Output

Here is a sample of the bacteria_count_data.json struct:

Bacteria Count Data Struct 
{
  "species": "Escherichia coli",
  "count": 12345,
  "location": "River A",
  "date": "2025-01-22"
}
